newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DISPUTED PENALTY GIVES REAL IMPORTANT WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DISPUTED PENALTY GIVES REAL IMPORTANT WIN.

text.p: Real Madrid took a giant step toward securing the Spanish league championship on Sunday by beating Valladolid 1-0 thanks to a disputed Davor Suker penalty.
With four games left, Real moved eight points clear of arch-rivals Barcelona, who face Celta Vigo on Monday.
Barcelona saw their own chances of ensuring Spain's second European Cup place boosted when rivals Deportivo Coruna and Real Betis were each held to home draws.
Real Madrid survived a disallowed goal and absorbed heavy pressure before the referee surprisingly awarded a penalty when striker Predrag Mijatovic collided with Valladolid's Juan Pena.
Pena was booked for the foul, Suker scored from the spot, and Valladolid were reduced to ten men shortly afterwards when Pena was sent off for another challenge.
The downside for Real were bookings for Suker and Mijatovic, which mean the Balkan strike-pair will miss next Saturday's game at Athletic Bilbao.
"The victory was a bit expensive," commented club captain Fernando Hierro.

Third-placed Deportivo Coruna trail Barcelona by four points after missing nearly a dozen clear chances and a late penalty from Brazilian-born midfielder Donato in a goalless game with struggling Sporting Gijon.
"I missed the clearest chance of all," lamented Donato, who had only just come on as a substitute when he took the spot-kick.
Deportivo stay a point ahead of Real Betis, who allowed neighbours Sevilla to score twice in the final five minutes of their frantic 3-3 draw on Saturday.
Six points behind Betis are champions Atletico Madrid, who survived a tough game at Real Sociedad to come out with a 1-1 draw.
Atletico's place in Europe next season is already secured, but the fight for Spain's other two UEFA Cup berths looks set to go to the last game of the season.

Tenerife -- semifinalists in the competition this year -- slipped up 1-0 at Espanyol but fellow contenders Athletic Bilbao won 2-1 at Extremadura and Valencia took an unexpected 2-0 win home with them from neighbours Hercules.
"I must ask for apologies ... they are a brotherly club," Valencia chairman Paco Roig said afterwards.
